summary: For the 2026 Space Apps Challenge, our team developed Lunar Base, a game designed to address the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Our game teaches young astronauts resource management, space exploration, and balancing goals by giving them real-world challenges faced by astronauts in space. They must manage power, grow food in the greenhouse, and monitor radiation in space. By combining engaging gameplay with educational concepts based off of NASA data, Lunar Base bridges the gap between complex science and interactive gameplay.
details:
Lunar base is an educational game where players set up and manage a sustainable base on the Moon. Players have to balance their resources while learning about lunar environmental factors. The project makes learning easily accessible to kids and students. It creates problem-solving skills, curiosity, and knowledge of real NASA missions. Our team used Python, Vercel, and Github. We also used tools like ChatGPT to help with coding logic and refining the game mechanics and design, as well as gathering a bit of information.
The game turns scientific concepts into mechanics in the game, such as the lunar weather and greenhouse research. Players can actively experience the challenges that an astronaut might face while playing this game. We focused on creating a kid-friendly app that balances educational accuracy with engaging gameplay to inspire the next generation of space explorers.
